subject.title: feat(gateway): add context engine control API

question: Should context-engine control be an HTTP-only endpoint with non-advertised scope checks, or a full advertised Gateway RPC surface with dispatch handlers and protocol docs?
rationale: The PR adds both HTTP routes and public core method descriptors, but only the HTTP route is implemented; choosing the permanent control-plane surface is a gateway/plugin API product and security-boundary decision.

options.title: Keep HTTP-only for now
options.body: Remove or hide the public `contextEngine.*` RPC advertisements, keep the HTTP bridge as the implemented surface, and document its route, scope, and payload contract.

options.title: Implement full RPC support
options.body: Add dispatchable Gateway RPC handlers, protocol docs, and tests for `contextEngine.capabilities`, `contextEngine.status`, `contextEngine.doctor`, and `contextEngine.rotate`.

options.title: Pause the feature
options.body: Close or pause this branch until maintainers settle the context-engine control API shape outside a dirty PR branch.

recommendation.title: Keep HTTP-only for now
recommendation.body: Remove or hide the public `contextEngine.*` RPC advertisements, keep the HTTP bridge as the implemented surface, and document its route, scope, and payload contract.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent gateway method-scope and descriptor work makes this the best routing candidate for the API-surface decision.
